source_evidence: If you die before you start receiving payments, the person you name as your beneficiary receives at least the current value of the annuity, perhaps more.
question: Misconception: An annuity’s death benefit always guarantees a beneficiary an amount greater than the annuity’s current value.
answer: Not necessarily. If you die before receiving payments, the beneficiary receives at least the annuity’s current value, and possibly more. Any additional amount depends on the contract; withdrawals may also reduce the death benefit, sometimes by more than the amount withdrawn.
